text: REMOVAL OF DEAD, DYING DISEASED THINNING TO MINIMIZE FIRE DANGER IN CONIFER FORESTS OF KHYBER PAKHTUNKHWA HIGH HILL MOIST TEMPERATE AND DRY TEMPERATE DEODAR, KAIL, FIR AND SPRUCE FORESTS In the province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa the common coniferous species are Deodar, Kail, Fir and Spruce in high hill moist temperate and dry temperate. The fire hazard in moist temperate are very rare while in dry temperate Deodar Forests though of less frequent than chir but its effects are much devastating. The main reason of fire in dry temperate forests of Deodar are the dry standing and wind fallen trees. It is always an uphill impossible task to extinguish fire in these forests until all the debris are burnt or heavy snowfall rains took place. The only remedial measure against the fire is the removal of dead, dying diseased trees from these forests. The following is the way forward for removal of dead, dying and diseased trees from High hill dry temperate and moist temperate forests. Preparation of compartment wise enumeration lists of all the dry, windfalls and diseased trees during the month of March by the SDFO RFO concerned with the assistance of concerned Beat Guard and Block Officer. The DFO will carry out proper marking associating the media personals, local bodies representatives and submit the lists to Conservator of Forests for approval of marking the dead, dying and diseased trees until 14 th of April. The Conservator of Forests will issue necessary order until 25th of April and the DFO will arrange for departmental conversion and transportation of the standing volume up to 10000 cft to the central Depot until 5th of May while for conversion of more than 10000 in Reserved Forests of Hazara and protected forest in Malakand open tender for conversion will be floated in print electronic media. The timber on receipt at Central timber Depot will be allotted lot number compartment wise as per respective Forest Compartment. The auction of timber will be carried out as per lease procedure laid down in Forest Mannual Vol III. The expenditures incurred on conversion, transportation and storage will be deducted from the sale proceed to the timber and the net sale proceed shall be apportioned as provided in Rule of Protected Forest Management Rules, 2005. CHIR FORESTS Chir Forests is the most common genus of the family Pinaceae and the largest family within the coniferales. It is a large genus with over 110 species worldwide. Chir Pine has very large natural zone of distribution in sub tropical regions of India and Pakistan and is found in outer ranges and principal valleys of Himalayas from 2000 ft to 6000 feet elevation. It is an evergreen gregarious tree, forming almost pure forests of considerable extent, although it can occur at upper and lower reaches mixed with other species. Chir pine has a marked tendency to form even aged stands of varying extent. In Hazara the most important chir forests are occurring in Siran valley 3000 ft to 6000 ft, followed by Haripur and Agror Tanawal valleys, while in Galies and Kaghan Forest divisions, it occupies small areas. The restoration of scientific management in Chir pine is need of the hours and it should be managed with its proper scientific way which is illustrated in the following manners Uniform Shelter Wood System Management System In In Chir Forests The uniform shelter wood system, the most suitable silvicultural system of management of Chir pine forests was first applied in Grewall s working plan for Lower Siran and Agror valley, and soon followed in other working plan too. During this period, almost all the working plan was similar in their basic outlines i.e, silvicultural prescriptions, proposals and suggestions. The application of the uniform system has generally been accepted as a successful treatment, keeping in view the light demanding character of the species and attainment of established regeneration through natural means. Continuity in the application of this system could be resulted in the development of even aged stands in different forest areas, particularly in Siran valley, considered to be the best Chir pine in Pakistan. The following common objectives of the management could be attained under the application of uniform shelter wood system Building up the growing stock towards normality i.e. transformation from irregularity towards regularity uniformity. Balanced age and size class distribution i.e more resistant to fire. To produce maximum yield on sustainable basis so as to earn maximum revenue for stat exchequer. To provide sustainable green jobs to the local community as to ensure best participation in practical management as well as protection against fire and thefts of green assets. To reduce the fire hazards through intensive care and handling of crop through involvement of local communities. Resin tapping could sustainably be harvested which results in extra revenue for government exchequer in Reserve forests and monitory benefit to owners in the Guzara forests. Functioning Of Periodic Blocks Under Uniform Shelter Wood System In this system the canopy is opened up uniformly over the entire compartment to get more or less even aged crop. The old crop is removed in succession felling and the regeneration is obtained from seeds shed by the seed bearers which are retained in the area for this purpose. Sometimes Natural Regeneration is supplemented with artificial planting. The old trees are removed in successive felling known as regeneration or seedling felling which extended over a period of years. The period during which regeneration gets established is known as regeneration period. According to the length of regeneration period, the total rotation period is divided into 4 blocks technically known as PERIODIC BLOCKS. Regeneration period is allotted to PB IV and if the rotation age of Chir Pinus roxburgii is 100 years then The periodic blocks contains crop ranging These areas comprise of regeneration in such areas felling has taken place and only mother trees 6 to 7 per acre are felled before shifting to PB II. PB II Comprises of a predominating middle aged to mature crop which will be due for felling only after 51 to 75 years. PB III Consists of largely young to middle aged crop in the age of 26 to 50 years. PB IV Composed of mother tree and after felling shift to PB I. Felling In Periodic Block IV Felling in these areas is carried out in two phases Seeding felling Final felling Seeding Felling About 18 to 20 trees per hectare are retained as seed bearers. Their number is more on southern and warmer aspects. Uniform spacing of these seed bearers is ensured. While selecting seed bearers, middle aged, healthy trees are preferred. Compact groups of regeneration up to 20 cm diameter, having a minimum area of 0.25 hectare are retained as a part of the future crop. Suitable gaps are created in the canopy so as to induce regeneration. Final Felling in PB IV These felling are undertaken only when the seedlings have attained a height of about 4 meters. All seed bearers are removed during final felling. Certain seed bearers may have to be retained as a safety measure in patches where regeneration is not up to the mark before felling the trees are lopped so as to minimize damage to the young crop. Care is also taken to avoid damage to the regeneration, during extraction operations. During final felling all unhealthy poles, saplings and seedlings with stunted growth shall also the removed. Thinning in PB II The uniform shelter wood system is the system in which the mature crop is removed in a series of operations. The first operation is called seeding felling and the last is the final felling. The other felling if any, are known as secondary felling. The shelter wood system is also called Seed Tree Method shelter wood compartment system or system of successive regeneration fellings. The regeneration occurs under a shelter wood which is removed in a final felling only after the natural regeneration has got established. The regeneration interval which is the interval between the seeding felling and the final felling in a particular area determines the degree of uniformity of the resulting crop. The various operations in a shelter wood system are Retaining 7 to 8 middle age mother trees per acre. Manipulating canopy for adequate light reaching on the forest floor. The young regeneration needs less light but as it goes in size the light requirement increases and therefore secondary felling mother trees are removed. Control burning for better regeneration in Chir pine and disposal of slash for reducing fire incidence, insect and pathogens attack. iv Thinning is defined as a felling made in an immature stand for the purpose of improving the growth and form of the trees that remain without permanently breaking the canopy. It is a treatment of forest crops whereby the number of trees growing in a stand is reduced. Thinning consists of a series of successive felling operation for a number of times before the crop matures. The interval between two succession felling may be fixed but it is dependent on the time required for canopy closure. Thinning is carried out in a crop after it reaches the sapling stage and continued up to the beginning of the regeneration period. The thinning principles are applicable to pure and even aged or nearly even aged crop or even aged groups of the trees in a crop. Thinning always increases spacing and decreases the number of trees per unit area. Most of the trees species are raised at a close spacing i.e. i. 2 Meter x 2 meter or ii. 3 meter x 2 meter. After five or ten years depending upon species and site conditions the canopy closes or root competition is so heavy that the plants are not able to grow unless they are thinned out. They are quite spaced for the crown as well as root development. PC-I STRENGTHENING OF DEMARCATION DIVISION NORTHERN FOREST REGION.II ABBOTTABAD (01.07.2025 to 30.06.2028) (3 Years) Cost: Rs. 96.46 million Prepared by Bilal A hmad Divisional F orest officer Demarcation F orest D ivision Abbottabad Forest Department Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Peshawar June 2025 Annexure-I PROJECT DIGEST 1 Name of the Project: Strengthening of Demarcation Division, Northern Forest Region. II Abbottabad 2 Location: The project shall be executed in the Northern Forest Region. II Abbottabad. The map is given as Annexure-I above. 3 Authorities responsible for: i . Sponsoring: Through Forest Development Fund ii. Execution: Climate Change, Forestry Environment and Wildlife Department iii. Operation & Maintenance Demarcation Forest Division, Northern Forest Region. II Abbottabad iv. Concerned Federal Ministry Ministry of Climate Change, Forestry Environment and Wildlife Department (a) Plan Provision: If the project is included in the Medium Term/Five Year Plan, specify the actual allocation The project is included in the Forest Development Fund at a cost of Rs. 96.46 million. The project shall be completed in three years subject to in-time provisions of funds as per approved PC-I. If not included in the medium-term/Five Year plan, what warrants its inclusion and how is it now proposed to be accommodated: The project is fully in line with MDG and Green Growth Initiatives. If the project is proposed to be financed out of block provision, indicate: N.A (b) Provision in the current year Forest Development Fund. Express Provision is made in the Forest Ordinance 2002 about generation and utilization of the FDF, hence the instant project is elaborated in accordance with the injunctions of the ibid Ordinance/Act and rules made thereunder. Project Objectives and its relationship with sector objectives: The objectives of the project are in consonance with the objectives laid down in Forest Ordinance 2002, FDF Rules 2025 and Forestry Sector. By addressing the following objectives, the project aims to achieve a harmonious balance between ecological conservation, community development and economic growth within the forestry sector; Objectives of the Project: Enhancing Forest Protection & Conservation: Strengthen the capacity of the Demarcation Division Northern Forest Region.II Abbottabad for effective protection and conservation of forests. Resultantly, it will help in removing encroachments and forest degradation through improved monitoring and enforcement mechanisms through the implementation of modern forest management techniques to ensure the sustainable use of forest resources. Boundary Demarcation & Legal Protection: Conduct a comprehensive survey to properly demarcate forest boundaries of designated forests i.e. reserved, protected and guzara forest to identify the exact boundaries and thereby to prevent encroachments. Erect permanent boundary pillars and signage for clear identification of forest land to resolve land disputes through legal and administrative measures in coordination with relevant authorities. Capacity Building & Institutional Strengthening: Enhance the capacity of the Demarcation Division by providing them with modern tools, GIS mapping systems and field equipment. Provision of specialized training programs for field staff in surveying, mapping, GIS applications and legal aspects of land protection. Recruitment/hiring of additional skilled personnel including GIS Analysts and GIS professionals, Girdawar and Patwari will be hired on a need basis under the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa project policy to accomplish the assigned task efficiently and accurately. Demarcation of Designated Forests: The designated forests specifically Protected and Guzara Forests do not have complete boundary pillars erected on the ground. As a result, their demarcation has led to settled possession disputes, unresolved mutations and discrepancies between revenue and forest records. While in case of Reserved Forests though demarcated by Survey of Pakistan, the issues emerging with passage of time i.e. encroachment, overlapping and ownership claim is also dealt by demarcation division to ascertain the factual position as per available record. The recent practice conducted in the Haripur Forest Division for identifying designated forests will serve as a precedent for future demarcation efforts in Northern Forest Region.II . Deployment of Technology for Monitoring & Reporting: Establishment of a GIS-based forest monitoring system for real-time tracking of forest health and encroachments. Use satellite imagery to enhance surveillance and documentation of forest cover changes. Development of a digital Forest Information Management System (FIMS) for better data collection, storage and decision-making. Infrastructure Development for Effective Field Operations: Provision of essential infrastructure, including vehicles, communication systems and survey equipment for efficient mobility and field operations. The above steps/measures will enable the Demarcation Forest Division, Northern Region II to identify, calculate the extent and prepare proper encroachment maps that will help in retrieving the existing encroachment areas and will protect the vulnerability of designated forest land from future encroachment. Description and justification, technical parameters and technology transfer aspects of the Project: Project Description: Demarcation Division Northern Forest Region-II Abbottabad was established in 2021 through an approved SNE to delineate and manage forest boundaries for sustainable use and protection of forest resources. The division operates with a sanctioned strength of 51 personnel, comprising Professional, Para-Professional, Ministerial, Technical and Class-IV staff. The Northern Forest Region.II faces persistent challenges due to historical land disputes, encroachments and ambiguities in forest boundary definitions, particularly in the case of Reserved Forests, Guzara Forests and Resumed Lands. These issues have resulted in unauthorized land use, illegal encroachments and conflicts, including disputes over mining rights and ownership claims. The lack of precise demarcation undermines sustainable forest management and the conservation of critical natural resources. A notable concern is the demarcation of Resumed Lands, across Haripur, Agror Tanawal and Hazara Tribal Forest Divisions. In some areas, the absence of clearly defined and legally recognized boundaries has made these lands susceptible to illegal occupation, unauthorized land use changes and conflicts among local stakeholders. The Strengthening Demarcation Division NFR-II Abbottabad project is a critical initiative to address long-standing boundary issues and promote sustainable forest management in the region. By leveraging advanced geospatial technologies and enhancing institutional capacity, the project will contribute to the long-term protection and conservation of forest resources, ensuring environmental sustainability and socio-economic stability for future generations. Project Justification Before going to project justification following are the main problems that need to be rectified. Lack of demarcation of designated forests, specially protected and guzara forests. Non-availability of authentic forest records. Non- updation of existing forest records. Missing links in existing forest records. Dichotomy in forest and revenue record resulting in the litigation. Absence/partially available or broken boundary pillars. Through the instant project, the following outcome will be achieved. Accurate Boundary Demarcation: Utilize advanced Geographical Information Systems (GIS) and land survey technologies, such as Differential Global Positioning Systems (DGPS) and total stations, to establish precise boundaries for Protected Forests, Guzara Forests and Reserved Forests. Establishment of a GIS Laboratory: Develop a state-of-the-art GIS Lab equipped with modern hardware and software to enable effective spatial data collection, transformation, analysis and dissemination. Strengthening Forest Administration: Enhance the capacity of the Forest Department to manage spatial data, monitor land use changes and make informed, data-driven decisions. Legal Reinforcement: Facilitate legal recognition of demarcated boundaries to prevent encroachments, resolve disputes and safeguard forest lands. Sustainable Resource Management: Promote sustainable management practices that align with international standards for geospatial data handling and forest conservation. Technical parameters: The details of activities along with physical and financial targets are given in Annexure-II. The following proposed interventions are designed to enhance geospatial capabilities, improve field data collection, ensure operational efficiency and promote safety. This comprehensive approach will significantly contribute to the effective management and demarcation of forest boundaries in NFR-II. Staffing and Management To ensure efficient and uninterrupted functioning of demarcation division Abbottabad, a dedicated team will be engaged. Upon successful completion of the project, the regularization of these positions will be initiated through SNE (Schedule of New Expenditures) formalization. S. text: INTRODUCTION AND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT The Working Plan is revision of Masood s Working Plan 02 to 2015 and is so the 4th revision of Working Plan for the Galis Guzara Forests of Galis Forest Division. The Working Plan aims at the management of forests on sustainable basis and consequent multiple use of the resource in sustainable manner through joint participatory management approach with active and informed participation of all stake holders. However special attention is given to the rehabilitation and invigoration of the existing forests. Total land area under the Working Plan is about 177,960 ha comprising all segments of areas under renewable natural resources and the corresponding land use classes found in the Planning Area. It deals with all land use classes found in the Planning Area like forests, agriculture, range lands and pastures with main focus on sustainable management of the Galies Guzara Forests, spreading over 8239 ha area, comprising 169 forest compartments compartments. The planning document also addresses the issue of climate change and its impacts on forest ecosystems, and combatting climate change impacts through adaptation and mitigation through carbon sequestration and storage as biomass in wood and wood products. Similarly, REDD mechanism is used as a tool for climate change mitigation and also provide an opportunity for maintaining and increasing national forest resources. The current revision was kicked up using Standardized Methodology for Resource Inventory Planning for field data collection. Then compilation, processing and analysis of the data were carried out for assessment and estimation of growing stock, productivity and growth of the forests for future strategy and management. After analysis of the data accompanied by other considerations and factors, the forests were categorized into three working circles, namely i Community Use Working Circle, ii Conservation Working Circle and iii tourism Working Circle, for their specific functions and role, and proper treatment prescribed for rehabilitation and invigoration of the forests accordingly. . The timely completion of this important and demanding assignment has become possible only that ALL MIGHTY ALLAH, the most Gracious, Beneficent and Merciful bestowed on me better health and mind, valor and courage and perception and intelligence enough to accomplish the task. The support and cooperation of DFO Galis Forest Division, his office staff and field staff as well, for provision of the required information documents, sparing time for meetings and company in field visits, deserve appreciation. I feel pleasure to express my heartiest gratitude to the Chief Conservator of Forests Mr. Azhar Ali, and the then Chief Conservators of Forests M S Muhammad Saddique Khattak, Niaz Ali Khan, and Ali Gohar for completion of the assignment under their vigorous patronage and guidance. I am highly indebted to Mr. Niaz Ali Khan the then Conservator of Forests Forestry Planning Monitoring Circle Peshawar for his vigilant supervision and who reposed confidence in me by delivering this important and highly technical assignment vide his Office Order No. 46 dated 21 2017. My special and heartfelt indebtedness goes to M S Tuheedul Haq and Syed Zakir Hussain Shah the then Conservators of Forests FP M Circle Peshawar for their tedious efforts, support, guidance and work friendly behavior which encouraged me to accomplish this highly important and technical assignment. I also appreciate the efforts and advices of Mr. Khurshid Ali Qureshi the Conservator of Forests Forestry Planning Monitoring Circle Peshawar which enabled me to complete the remaining drafting up of the Resource Management Plan during the current calendar year 2021. I take the opportunity to bring on record the hard work, patience and spirit of diligence evinced by M S Muhammad Touqeer Mir, Muhammad Zahid, Muhammad Yasir, Shahzad Ahmad, Abdul Sattar, Gul Siraj Foresters and Syed Hamad Hussain Shah, Alam Zeb, Sajjad Ahmad Forest Guards. Zahid Aamir Driver Nisar Khan Naib Qasid during the course of field work. For data processing, compilation and assistance in drafting work, the credit goes to Mr. Muhammad Touqeer Mir Forester. All the concerned communities, public servants and other forest friendly people are paid special thanks in the hope of raising at least their voices in support of forestry. May All Mighty Allah enable all concerned stake holders to make endeavors to implement the Plan effectively so as to achieve the goal of sustainable Forest Management. text: I REHABILITATION AND IMPROVEMENT OF DIFFERENT CATCHMENT AREAS OF DAMS HYDROPOWER STATIONS LOCATED IN HAZARA 01.07.2023 to 30.06.2028 Rs. 9919.515 million Forest Department Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Peshawar Annex PC I PROJECT DIGEST 1 Name of the Project Rehabilitation And Improvement Of Different Catchment Areas Of Dams Hydropower Stations Located In Hazara Location The project extends to the entire Hazara Division as well as that part of Malakand which drains into River Indus. The program is being implemented by the Watershed Management Circle of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Forest Department. The Circle Project area map is at Annex Authorities responsible For Sponsoring The instant project will be implemented in the Watershed Management Circle of Northern Forest Region, Hazara and sponsored through ADP for ensuring conservation and sustainability of the resources developed there under. Execution The Govt. of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Forest Department through Project Director Conservator of Forests, Watershed Management Circle, under the overall administrative control of the Secretary Forestry, Environment and Wildlife Department Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The maintenance of the activities will be executed through the Watershed managerial staff of Watershed Circle under the overall control of Chief Conservator of Forests Northern Forest Region, Hazara. The sisters departments will provide the requisite support for implementation of project in accordance with their approved mandate provision of PC 1exclusively in consultation with respective Chief Conservator of Forests and provision of PC Operation Maintenance Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Forest Department Concerned Federal Ministry Water Resources Plan Provision If the project is included in the Medium Term Five Year Plan, specify actual allocation Project Description Location of project indicate place administrative district and attach map . The project area is located KPK and extends over an area of 18230 sq km covering Haripur , Abbottabad, Mansehra, Battagram, Kohistan, Torghar, Shangla and Buner districts. For management purposes and based on the watersheds of the tributaries draining into main rivers, the project area has been divided into five Divisions, as shown in table. Project area division wise Watershed Division Sub Divisions Tributaries Draining into Catchment area of Area Sq km Percentage of total Abbottabad, Havelian, Sherwan Tarbela reservoir Battagram, Allai, Shergarh, Torghar Unhar, Nandair and AllaiKhawar GhariHabibullah, Balakot, Bakote and Siran Kunhar and Siran SukiKinari,Balakot,Mangla and Tarbela reservoirs Kohistan Besham, Kohistan, Puran Indus, Alpuri Khawar Dasu, Bhasha and Tarbela reservoir Dagger, Pacha, Chamla Tarbela reservoir During this project phase, the geographical area of the project will be maintained without any changes and no other project should overlap its jurisdiction. The area falls in the active monsoon and receding rainfall zone and contributes 30 40 percent of the silt load carried annually to Tarbela Mangla reservoirs, in spite of the fact that this forms only 10 of the total catchment of the reservoir falling within the jurisdiction of Pakistan. The total catchment of Tarbela and Mangla reservoirs is about 36260 sq km making the project area is hardly 5 of the total. However, proper land use treatment of this area is extremely important because the area falling in active monsoon contributes 40 of the silt load. As regards other 60 silt load, major part of it comes from area beyond the territorial boundaries of Pakistan, therefore, very little can be done about that, Moreover, the sediment load coming beyond the active monsoon zone within and outside Pakistan is mostly geologic in origin therefore, no human efforts can arrest it. The project attempts through its measures in afforestation and soil conservation to contribute sustainably to ecological stabilization in its zone of activity. Hydrologically the country can be divided into three main units i.e. the Indus basin, closed basin of Kharan desert and Makran coastal basin. The Indus basin covering some 360,000 sqkms is the largest of all. Besides its main tributaries in the Punjab, the Indus is also drained into by river Kabul and its main tributaries Swat, Chitral, Punjkora, Kurram and Gomal rivers. Pakistan is generally a dry country of hot dry sub tropical and temperature climatic zones. Great climatic variations prevail from northern mountains down to coastal plains in the southern regions. The general climatic character is that of arid. Annual precipitation except in northern hilly areas averages less than 250 mm, decreasing from northern to southern regions. The climatic zonation of the country is given in Table 3. Table Climatic zonation of Pakistan Area million acres Province Semi arid Sub humid Balochistan The above climatic zonation of the country indicates that the area falling in the northern regions of the country and within KPK is vital water providing areas for agricultural economy of Pakistan i.e. irrigated plains of Sindh and Punjab. Similarly for generation of hydro power, operations of industries and rural electrification, this watershed area are vital national importance. Besides either sources of energy, Pakistan has to rely greatly on its natural resources and their sustained scientific management. Substantial evidence of environmental degradation exists in the northern region of the country. The process of ecological deterioration in terms of soil erosion, siltation of dams reservoirs, water courses and flash floods can be observed throughout the mountainous areas of the country especially during monsoon. Increasing pressure of human population and livestock on natural resources, excessive fallings of trees and overgrazing are the major causes of environmental degradation. Pakistan is the fifth most populous country the World, with population growth rate of over 2.21 percent per annum and a per capita GNP of 1562 US dollar. During in accordance with international standards, Pakistan is recognized as low income and food deficit country. Increase in population and lack of job opportunities have resulted in migration, labour force to Gulf countries and big cities like Karachi, Hyderabad, and Lahore etc. This has created many socio economic problems. Pressure on the natural resources has tremendously increased. Over the last three decades, indiscriminate tree felling occurred in reserved, protected and private forests. The accelerated soil erosion and gully formation often causes land slides in the hilly areas. The downward movement of sedimentation causes damage to lowland agriculture and rapid siltation of irrigation system particularly reservoirs and water distribution system. The people inhabiting the project area are generally poor and illiterate. The symptoms of malnutrition, poor health and unemployment are very common. Due to lack of education and financial support, they themselves cannot ameliorate their lot. For scores of reasons the people offer resistance to change and continue to pursue their conventional farming practices on small marginal and non profitable holdings. The social institutional infrastructure such as community centres are almost nonexistent in the villages. The traditional Hujra are fast disappearing. The development works executed by the Government departments without contribution and involvement of the locals lack sustainability. The transhumance population also threatens the fragile ecology of this area. In summer thousands of nomad families alongwith their livestock visit alpine pastures and on their way cause damage both to the forests as well as to newly established plantations. For this, some reforms and political decisions are required to be taken in determining their routes and establishment of permanent camping sites. The social organizing team and other staff will try to motivate them for transportation of their livestock through trucks. This will serve dual purpose. On one side energy will be saved by reducing fatigue, while on the other side damage to young afforestations as well as, forests will be minimized. The prevailing land tenure system and laws of inheritance under which cultivated lands are fragmented to un economic holdings also contribute towards poor management of watershed areas. Present 79 percent of the farms are fragmented. Farm of size less than five acres are more than 60 percent in Hazara and 34 percent in Swat. Since 1947, the size of average farm has decreased from 8.2 acres to 3.1 acres. The phenomenon of breaking of now waste lands and abandonment of cultivation on denuded slopes and broken terraces are not uncommon. This causes severe soil erosion and floods in lying plain districts of the country. About 70 percent or the population falls short of food sufficiency. The Government attempts to provide food grains to the locals on subsidized rates through the policy of support process. Some of the people sell their surplus food grains in the market to meet their emergent requirements. Seventy five percent of the farms are operated by the owners only 25 percent are owners cum tenant operated. According to land capability classification the project area be grouped as under Land capability class 1, 1I, 10 and P1, includes land under cultivation. Land capability class VI, viz constitutes grassland and forests. Land capability class Vol comprising unproductive waste. Land capability class VIII comprises of alpine pastures and meadows. The land use statistics are at variance in different reports, however, waste land comprising of range land and alpine pastures constitute about 42 percent of the total project area. About 50 percent of the wastelands 81,206 acres are considered to be suitable for afforestation activities. Part III and IV will be filled by the Reporting Officer while the countersigning Second Countersigning Officers will fill Parts V and VI respectively. The ratings in Part III should be recorded by initiating the appropriate box. Each Division, Department, autonomous body and office etc. is required to prepare specific job descriptions giving main duties of each job to be mentioned in Part . The job descriptions may be finalized with the approval of the Head of the Organization or any person authorized by him. The officer under report should fill Part of the form as objectively as possible and short term and long term targets should be determined assigned with utmost care. The targets for each job may be formulated at the beginning of the year wherever possible. In other cases, the work performed during the year needs to be specifically mentioned. Assessment by the Reporting Officers should be job specific and confined to the work done by the officer during the period under report. They should avoid giving a biased or evasive assessment of the officer under report, as the Countersigning Officers would be required to comment on the quality of the assessment made by them. The Reporting Officers should support their assessment in Part IV through comments against each characteristic. Their opinions should represent the result of careful consideration and objective assessment so that, if called upon, they could justify the remarks comments. They may maintain a record of the work done by the subordinates in this regard. The Countersigning Officers should weigh the remarks of the RO against their personal knowledge of the officer under report and then give their assessment in Part VG. Similarly, if the countersigning Officers differ with the grading or remarks given by the Reporting Officer in part III they should scare it out and give their own grading by initiating the appropriate box. The counter signing Officers should make an unbiased evaluation of the quality of performance evaluation made by the RO by categorizing the reports as exaggerated, fair or biased. This would evoke a greater sense of responsibility from the reporting officers. The countersigning Officers should underline, in red ink, remarks, which in their opinion are adverse and should be communicated to the officer reported upon. All adverse remarks whether remediable or irremediable should be communicated to the officer under report, with a copy of communication placed in the CR dossier. Reporting Officers should ensure that proper counseling is given to the officer under report before adverse remarks are recorded. Reports should be consistent with the pen picture, overall grading and comparative grading. Short title and commencement: - (1) These rules may be called the 2[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa] Civil Servants (Appointment, Promotion and Transfer) Rules, 1989. (2) They shall come into force at once. 2. Definitions:-(1) In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires:- (a) "Appointing Authority" in relation to a post, means the persons authorized under rule 4 to make appointment to that post; (b) "Basic Pay Scale" means the Basic Pay Scale for the time being sanctioned by Government, in which a post or a group of posts is placed; (c) "Commission" means the 3[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa] Public Service Commission; 4(d) "Departmental Promotion Committee" means a committee constituted for making selection for promotion or transfer to such posts under a Department, or offices of Government, which do not fall within the purview of the Provincial Selection Board; 5(dd)"Departmental Selection Board" means a Board constituted for the purpose of making selection for initial recruitment /appointment to posts under a Department or office of Government in Basic Pay Scale 17 not falling within the purview of the Commission: Provided that more than one such committees may be constituted for civil servants holding different scales of pay". (e) "Departmental Selection Committee" means a committee constituted for the purpose of making selection for initial appointment to posts under a department, or office of Government [in Basic Pay Scale 17 and below not falling within the purview of the Commission]; (f) "Post" means a post sanctioned in connection with the affairs of the Province, but not allocated to all Pakistan Unified Grades ; and 1 For the words “NWFP” or “North-West Frontier Province”, wherever occurred, the words “Khyber Pakhtunkhwa” substituted by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Laws (Amendment) Act, 2011 (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Act No. IV of 2011) published in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Government Gazette Extraordinary dated 2nd April, 2011 2 Sub.by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Act No. IV of 2011. 3 Sub.by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Act No. IV of 2011. 4 Substituted by Clause (d) of sub-rule (1) of Rule 2 vide Notification No. SOR-I (S&GAD) 4-1/80 (Vol-II) dated 14-01-92. 5 Clause (dd) added by Notification No. SOR-III (S&GAD) 2-7/86, dated 8-12-1994 6(g) “Provincial Selection Board" means the Board constituted by Government for the purpose of selection of civil servants for promotion or transfer to posts in respect whereof the appointing authority under rule 4 is the Chief Minister and shall consist of such persons as may be appointed to it by Government from time to time. (2) Words and expressions used but not defined in these rules shall have the same meanings as are assigned to them in the 7[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa] Civil Servants Act, 1973 (8[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa] Act XVIII of 1973) or any other statutory order or rules of Government for the time being in force. 3. Method of Appointment:- (1) Appointment to posts shall be made by any of the following methods, namely:- (a) by promotion or transfer in accordance with the provisions contained in Part-II of these rules; and (b) by initial recruitment in accordance with the provisions contained in Part-III of these rules. text: NON ADP SCHEME I TEN BILLION TREE TSUNAMI PROGRAMME PHASE SCALING OF GREEN PAKISTAN PROGRAMME 01.07.2019 to 30.06.2023 Rs. 27339.700 million 27 billion Forest Department Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Peshawar June 28, 2019 Annexure I Form PROJECT DIGEST 1 Name of the Project Ten Billion Tree Tsunami Programme Phase I, Up scaling of Green Pakistan Programme Location The project shall be executed in entire Khyber Pakhtunkhwa which includes Ex. Fata comprising 25 districts which are covered by 35 Forest and Watershed Divisions of Southern Central Region, Northern Forests Region II and Malakand Region III. The total forest area of the province after merger of Ex FATA is 2,636,475 hectares. The Regions and Forest Divisions map is at Annexure I. The exact locations of the activities shall, after GPS measurements be incorporated in the maps of the Divisions. Authorities responsible for Sponsoring The instant project is subset of the overall National 10 Billion Tree Planting Project to be executed in all the federating units with financial assistance of the Federal Government. The contribution of the Province through ADP and Federal Government through PSDP shall be 50 Execution Under the overall administrative control of the Secretary Forestry, Environment and Wildlife Department Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa the project shall be executed under following arrangements At Federal level The Ministry of Climate Change for arranging funds and affording support through appointment of fulltime Project Coordinator At Provincial level Project Director assisted by Project Management Unit coordination and monitoring Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Forest Department Execution of physical activities The Integrated Specialized Units provision of the requisite support for accomplishment of the process envisaged for execution of physical activities in order to attain higher prospects of sustainability. Operation Maintenance Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Forest Department and beneficiary communities Concerned Federal Ministry Ministry of Climate Change Plan Provision If the project is included in the Medium Term Five Year Plan, specify actual allocation Although, the project is not included in the Medium Term Five Year Plan as such, but it is positively related to the overall objectives set forth in the MTDF for conservation, improvement and rehabilitation of forest ecosystems. The project will not only help conservation of the natural forests through direct interventions but also expand forest resource base contributing towards building livelihoods as well as mitigating the adversities of climate change. The project will pave way for smooth transformation of current economic growth model to that of the Green Economy. It has now been widely realized that the existing global growth model by costing natural resources whereupon the rural economy is based, has hardly helped poverty reduction. Thus, in order to deliver socially inclusive, environmentally sustainable and climate resilient development, new economic growth model called Green Economy is being promoted worldwide. The categorical announcements of Prime Minister Pakistan and Chief Minister Khyber Pakhtunkhwa reveal strong commitments of allocating financial resources and affording other required facilities for execution of the instant project. The government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Forest Department has successfully completed the renowned Billion Tree Afforestation Project developed under the Green Growth Initiative . The marvelous achievements made under BTAP in terms of contributing towards addition of 6 forest cover and rehabilitating stock density of 20 natural forests besides creating job opportunities for hundreds of thousands local people, give confidence to scale up the initiative generally with same modalities throughout the country by using available vast land and human resources. The project shall be completed in five years with total cost of Rs. 27339 Millions. ii If not included in the medium term Five Year plan, what warrants its inclusion and how is it now proposed to be accommodated The project is fully in line with MDG and Green Growth Initiatives. The climate change challenges warrant immediate response by embarking on green projects. Keeping in view the strong commitments of the government on all stages, the project shall be executed by adjusting allocations in PSDP and Provincial ADP If the project is proposed to be financed out of block provision, indicate N.A 4 Provision in the current year PSDP The project is reflected in PSDP for the year 2019 20 and also included in ADP for the year 2019 20. 5. Project Objectives and its relationship with sector objectives In Pakistan, as per the forest classifications by the functions and types, there are 42.8 coniferous, 37.8 scrubs, 6.5 Riverine, 7.6 mangrove, 5.1 irrigated plantations and 0.4 linear plantations. Out of total 4.579 million hectare forest cover, only 1.266 million hectare is productive. These forests and rangelands are scattered over 60 of the country partly supporting about 100 million head of livestock. According to Landsat based assessment of forest cover change, the annual rate of deforestation in natural forests is estimated to be around 27,000 ha. Unfavorable climatic conditions, rural poverty dependence on the natural resources, meager forest cover and high rate of deforestation has rendered the country one of the most vulnerable to climates change effects. According to climate Risk Index developed by German Watch, Pakistan is 7th most vulnerable country to ill effects of climate change. Between the provinces, the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is comparatively rich in forest cover. The precious coniferous forest growing on upland watersheds in Malakand and Hazara Civil Divisions and Ex FATA play critical role in regulating country s irrigation system, maintaining ecology and meeting livelihoods of millions of dependants. Unfortunately, due to immense pressure of wood acquisition for fuel and construction more than 70 of these forests are rendered depleted. Studies show that status of regeneration in 76 of these forests is very unsatisfactory due to free grazing and persistent fire occurrence Government of KP Provincial Forest Resource Inventory . The drain of fuelwood acquisition is the main factor responsible of forest deterioration, Forest Department Fuelwood per capita as well as total outsource consumption in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa . According to this report, out of 15.532 million m3 fuelwood consumed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 32 is procured from the Forests. It is feared that the entire natural forest may vanish in the mid of century if corrective and curative measures in shape of plantation on wastelands, rehabilitation of depleted forests etc. are not done timely. Further, to meet food requirements of ever increasing local population, besides encroaching upon these forests, the steep slopes are converted into fields for tillage. The situation of Ex FATA is not an exception due to militancy and dependence of locals on natural resources is causing continuous depletion of the forests. Despite all of such bleak pictures, there are ample opportunities to regenerate these forests if nature in given a chance by minimizing human disturbances. Out of the total 2.043 million hectares area of province, 20 forest cover. More than 25 land is available for plantations to minimize pressure on the existing forest and meeting domestic needs and creating livelihood opportunities of the communities. Recently the province has successfully completed BTAP whereby 6 additional land of the province has been brought under forests besides assisting natural regeneration in 20 of existing forests. As the area of the province is increased by inclusion of Ex FATA, therefore the potential for increasing the forest cover has further increased for realizing the objectives set forth. Therefore the targets of the instant project are accordingly fixed. Further, the project will help realization of the objectives set forth in the Forest Policy 1999 regarding meeting needs of fuel wood and timber for domestic needs, affording job opportunities in green sector, enhancing protective functions of the watersheds, introducing effective range management regimes, conserving biological diversity, fostering attitudinal change in the communities in support of forest management and assisting government in fulfilling the international treaties. 6. Description and justification, technical parameters and technology transfer aspects of the Project 6.1 Project Description The instant project is part of federal government s 10 billion plantation program. The KP government to the extent of its share, shall adopt the initiative as program. The instant project is designed for 5 years whereas the remaining targets of 10 billion project shall be achieved in next 5 years. In this part of the program one billion plants shall be added in the KP by assisting natural regeneration and Afforestation. As mentioned in the previous sections the forests of the province are under tremendous pressure owing fuel wood and timber acquisition. Such pressure has rendered most of the forests of poor and medium density wanting restocking on war footings. Mostly these forests are situated in Hazara, Malakand and Ex. FATA. Success prospects of rehabilitation of such depleted forests by assisting natural regeneration are highly promising as favour of nature in growth of these forests is already established. These forests shall be restocked by restoring undisturbed natural conditions mandatory for natural regeneration. For this purpose enclosures of appropriate size averagely 40 hectares each, shall be established by appointment of Nigahbans who will be responsible to protect the enclosed forests against fire occurrence and grazing, which are the main factors obstructing natural regeneration. text: PART – I SUMMARY OF THE FACTS ON WHICH PROPOSAL ARE BASED CHAPTER – 1 DESCRIPTION OF THE TRACT DEALT WITH GENERAL This Working Plan is the 4 th Revised Working Plan for Galis Guzara Forests. The present revision has become due on account of the expiry of the Qazi Masaood -Ur-Rahman's Plan. Total area under the Plan is about 177,981 ha comprising all segments of areas under renewable natural resources and the corresponding land use classes found in the Planning Area. It deals with forests, agriculture, range lands and pastures with main focus on the sustainable management of the Galis Guzara Forests spread over the whole Abbottabad district. The concept of integrated and sustainable Natural Resource Management with active participation of all the stake holders is the core theme of the Plan. The GIS techniques were utilized for preparation of boundary location Maps, compartment grid Maps, site location Maps, land cover/use Maps, activities Maps, Management Map etc. Further planning including Operational Plans, Joint Forest Management Plans and Village Plans at their appropriate level will be carried out for implementation of the Working Plan. These supplementary Plans will be prepared with close consultations and active participation of the local communities. The goal and objectives as envisaged in the Plan could be achieved only through complete and full implementation of the Plan. This could be possible only through practical participation of the local communities both at planning and execution stages. In this scenario the major role will be played by the local communities while forest department will act as technical and supervisory agency to bring the natural resources under Sustainable Management. In order to get the desired results and benefits on sustainable basis, the Plan requires to be implemented in true spirit keeping in view the ground realities and integrated and Joint Management Approach. In this regard full and complete implementation will be the pivot point and incomplete or partial implementation shall be discouraged as practiced in the past. All the prescribed and proposed activities are to be executed as far as possible. 1.2 NAME AND LOCATION OF THE PLANNING AREA The Plan Area covers an area of about 177,981 ha, comprising all renewable natural resources and the corresponding land use classes found therein. It deals with forests, agriculture, range lands and pastures, habitation and other infra structures; however the focal land use class and pivot of management shall be Galis Guzara Forests spread over an area of 8239 ha . (Appendix 1 (b)) . The Guzara Forests are under administrative control of Galis Forest Division and spread over the whole Abbottabad district and are located between 33 o - 29’ and 34 o – 21' North latitudes and 72 o - 55'' and 73 o - 29' East longitudes. The Northern limits of the planning tract are bounded by Mansehra District, the Eastern by Jhelum River, and Southern & Western by Haripur District. The Guzara Forests form parts of Sub Divisions Abbottabad, Thandiani , Dung Gali and Bagnoter , and Biran Gali Range and are loacated on the range of hills running in north eastern, western and south-western direction of the prettiest hill resort of Abbottabad. The hill station Murree lies on the south-eastern side of the Guzara Forests. The towns of Mansehra and Havillian in the proximity of the forests while Nathia Gali, Donga Gali, Kalabagh and Thandiani hill stations are located in the vicinity of these forests. CONFIGURATION OF THE PLANNING AREA 1.3.1 Relief Most part of the Planning Area is mountainous with altitudinal variations ranging from about 454 meter above mean sea level (MSL) at Bir to 2977-meter-high peak of Miranjani . All the guzaras except those found in Abbottabad Sub-Division are situated on steep and precipitous slopes around the Galis Reserved Forests while Guzaras in Abbottabad Sub-Division present themselves in scattered patches with fragmented nature spreading over a series of low-lying hills frequently interrupted by a number of lateral spurs, nullahs and water courses creating a number of sub-valleys and side valleys. The topography is resultantly diverse in nature, comprising valleys and gullies and watersheds of varying size and gradient with its western part forming the catchment of Tarbela reservoir while North-Eastern part form watershed of the Mangla reservoir while the extreme South drains into Haro River. 1.3.2 Slope Most part of the Planning Area is mountainous with steep to moderately steep slopes. The slopes vary in degree of steepness they are generally steep to precipitous with occasional occurrence of easy and undulating ground near the tops of ridges and on spurs. Aspect Frequent variations occur in aspect due to multiplicity of ridges and their sub-divisions as offshoots. The Forests are generally better-stocked on northern and eastern aspects as compared to southern and western. The limiting factors in such areas are the non-availability of adequate moisture and nutrients to promote growth and help establish tree cover on shallow and shallow-rocky soils. 1.4 GEOLOGY AND ROCKS The geological formation of the tract is under continuous influence of the mountain building movements with Per-Eocene and Eocene zones conspicuously recognized. They consist of a series of limestone and slates, intruded by biotite and granite in the north eastern limits of the tract whereas meta-morphic series of phyletis , schist and granites are present in northern part. In the western part, Grey and purple sand stone with red and purple shale with rich deposits of soap stone are found. SOIL Most of the soil is grey in colour (under moist forests) and coarse in texture. The soil is formed by snow deposits as well as water and sedimentary rock and is mostly dry-farmed for subsistence cropping. Soil on the whole is moderately deep to fairly deep except on some overgrazed and degraded sites. Farm soil may be classified into four categories:- Loam and clay, mainly non-calcareous. Loam, steep and shallow soils (humid mountainous region). Loam and clay, partly non-calcareous with loess traces; and. Loam with stones, and shallow (sub-humid mountain region). The mountain ridges and terraces lying on the western and eastern boundaries of the district are severely eroded as a result of landslides, landslips, rock falls and debris flows. Inceptisols and chromudertic soils are the most common soil types found in the district. The inceptisols form level, productive basin plains, while the chromed ertic soils form piedmonts and undulated, dissected gullied lands. The soils of Ayubia and Bagnotar range from humid to sub-humid tropical continental. The following are the major soil types found in the planning area, composition and characteristics mentioned as under. Table No. 1 Soil Types Type Complex Composition and Characteristics 8 Rockland, Bagnotar and Makhnial Complex Exposed bad rock, Slightly gravelly silt loams, brown/black, non calcareous 9 Rockland Makhnial Complex Exposed bed rock, Slightly gravelly silt loams, black to very dark grayish brown, calcareous 10 Rockland, Kohala Baghpur Complex Exposed bed rock, lightly shally or silt loams, dark reddish brown to dark brown 13 Rockland, Baghpur and Baragali Exposed rock, slightly gravelly silt loams, shally loams, weakly structured on the shales and phyllites 17 Besham , Rockland, Makhnial , Sherwan , Phagora Slightly gravelly loams, shally or slaty sandy loams, on non calcarious phyllites etc. 18 Sherwan , Baragali Makhnial Complex Gravelly loams, slightly gravelly silt loams on sandstones etc. Exposed bedrock. 20 Sherwan Baragali Complex Gravelly loams, dark brown, slightly gravelly silt loams on shales and phyllites. Exposed bedrock 23 Rockland Phagora Complex Exposed bedrock, shaly or slaty silt loams yellowish brown CLIMATE The climate of the tract ranges from dry sub-tropical in a few low-lying areas situated west of Abbottabad to temperate over a major portion of the tract in the high altitudes. The area lying between 3000' to 9750' have temperate climate with marked seasonal periods of snow, rain and drought. The summar is moderate, while winter is severe with heavy snowfall usually occuring from mid-December to the end of February some times to the middle of March. It often accumulates on cooler and sheltered aspects up to the end of April. The higher reaches, are covered with snow till the end of April but disappears soon in areas below 5000' elevation. Part of the area to the west of Abbottabad having dry sub-tropical climate, receives comparatively less rain and remains dry for most of the year. January and February are the coldest months while March and April being pleasant, May and June are the hottest and dry months. Monsoon rains start usually in July and continue up to the end of August sometime up to the middle of September followed by a dry spell for about two months. Rain Fall Abbottabad district lies within the active monsoon zone and most of the rain occurs during Monsoon viz, July-August. The spring and autumn are the periods of less rain and often of drought. Most of the land is rain-fed, with 40% of average precipitation received during the July–August period and the remaining 60% unevenly distributed between September and June as tabulated below. text: INFORMATION SECURITY Often referred to as InfoSec. The processes and tools designed and deployed to protect sensitive business information from modification, disruption, destruction, and inspection. • Applies to digital and physical data • Essential for organizations and individuals GOALS OF INFORMATION SECURITY Protect sensitive information  Maintain trust and reputation  Ensure business continuity  Comply with legal and regulatory requirements  Organizations implement security controls to protect data and maintain operational stability. INFORMATION SECURITY CHALLENGES End User:  End users (that use our information systems) are prone to clicking on website URLs and launching attachments in emails Malware Kits:  Paying hackers for DIY kits to easily develop your own malware Cloud Computing:  Cheap and easy access to computing resources helps to ensure easy access to processing power Exploit Subscription Services:  Underground services that an attacker can subscribe to, to get the latest exploits EVOLUTION OF CYBERCRIME 1970s:  Phreaking (Telephone system) 1988:  Morris Worm 1989:  Ransomware 1990s:  Phishing attacks, Email etc EVOLUTION OF CYBERCRIME The 2000s brought us social media and saw the rise of identity theft.  A bullseye was painted for cybercriminals with the creation of  databases containing millions of users' personal identifiable information (PII), making identity theft the new financial bank for criminal organizations around the world. Today we have botnets, which are a network of private computers  that are infected with malicious software and allow the criminal element to control millions of infected computer systems across the globe. EVOLUTION OF CYBERCRIME THE MODERN ROLE OF INFORMATION SECURITY IT Security Engineering:  The application of security principles to information  technology. Information Assurance:  The act of working with business and IT leadership to ensure  that the confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements for a given asset are fully understood. THE CIA TRIAD Core foundation of Information Security Confidentiality  Integrity  Availability  The CIA Triad represents the three fundamental objectives of security systems. CONFIDENTIALITY It has to do with whether or not information is kept  secret or private. Ensures information is accessible only to  authorized users. Prevents unauthorized disclosure of data.  Examples: Encryption, passwords, access control. INTEGRITY It has to do with whether the information is kept  accurate. Information should not be modified in an  unauthorized manner and safeguards should be put in place that allows for detectable and timely unauthorized changes. Examples: Hashing, digital signatures, version control.

text: Attack An attack occurs when a threat actively exploits a vulnerability. Deliberate attempt to exploit vulnerabilities Can be passive or active Targets confidentiality, integrity, or availability In our modern era, human interaction is a key vector used to exploit an information system. Whether you are looking at attacks such as ransomware , or exploits against critical infrastructure , the easiest avenue into a system is by tricking the user to run a piece of software . The key way that we can make sure that our users are prepared for these attacks is by implementing an effective training and awareness program. Training Consider the value of the information that your organization owns. Consider what would happen to the organization if you lost control over the confidentiality , integrity , and/or availability of the information: A policy needs to take into account the organization's appetite for accepting risk: Answers to questions like these, combined with an understanding of you organizations risk appetite, will inform your policy development. Policies Are you trying to safeguard trade secrets or sensitive proprietary information (confidentiality )? Does information need to be accurate at all times (integrity )? Could the organization effectively operate without its information (availability)? There are many ways that a security standard can be met, and your policies should reflect the way that your organization wants to implement a standard Do not describe four points in a policy if you intend to only implement two of them if those two provide adequate risk mitigation Ensure your policies are implementable: Policies When developing a policy, you should ensure that you follow a few key principles : Receive board-level / CEO approval and support: Without CEO or board-level backing, a security program is doomed to fail You should only create a policy that you intend to follow: This means do not create a policy for the sake of the documentation . A policy that sits on the shelf and is never used does not help anyone. Policies that you don't follow will be used by an auditor to show that you are deficient : Policies A policy is a foundational aspect to the development of a strong information security program. If you have policies follow them. The PCI Data Security Standard ( DSS ) provides a framework for developing a payment card data security process, which includes prevention, detection, and incident response to security incidents. Mandatory requirement for any organization processing payment card data. PCI DDS Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (DSS) A training and awareness program will be the primary mechanism used to communicate organizational user roles and responsibilities from an information security perspective : Key Components of an Effective T raining and A wareness P rogram An effective training and awareness program is necessary to ensure successful implementation of your information security program. Secondary media products Primary media products Yearly information security awareness training Events This includes things like giveaways ( squeezy balls), alert notifications , posters, or social media. These serve to remind users about information security principles that you are communicating through other mechanisms. The key here is to keep information brief and manageable. If you need to read for more than ten seconds, it is too long. Secondary Media Products This includes things such as email newsletters, websites, and inclusions in corporate magazines. These have more contact and are distributed on a periodic basis. The key here is to not overwhelm the user. If you send out an email newsletter every week, you may find your newsletter in the spam folder . Secondary Media Products Threat A threat represents anything that can cause harm to information assets. Potential cause of an unwanted incident Can exploit system vulnerabilities May be internal or external This includes lunch time presentations, webinars, and presenting at corporate , divisional, or team meetings It is very important to deliver the information security message to your organization in person where possible: Webinars are useful in geographically-distributed organizations Getting 15 minutes to speak at the finance or HR teams quarterly meeting is a great way to answer questions that an entire group may have. Events This training should include a mechanism to test the users‘ understanding: The test should not be an information security vocabulary test: The user should know not to click on URLs and attachments they do not trust The user does not need to be test on the difference between phishing or spear phishing Use the yearly training as an opportunity to have your users validate or revalidate their acceptance of your organization's acceptable use policy: The training should cover every aspect of the Acceptable Use Policy Yearly Information Security Awareness Training This is training provided every year, where you communicate all of your information security requirements for the user into a single presentation The preferred method for implementing this training is computer-based, through a learning management system : Yearly Information Security Awareness Training This helps you to easily record users that have completed training and their scores The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 required the secretary of the U.S. department of Health and Human Services ( HHS ) to develop regulations protecting the privacy and security of certain health information. To fulfill this requirement, HHS published the HIPAA Privacy Rule and the HIPAA Security Rule . The Privacy Rule, or standards for privacy of individually identifiable health information, establishes national standards for the protection of certain health information. The security standards for the protection of electronic protected health information (the Security Rule) establish a national set of security standards for protecting certain health information that is held or transferred in electronic form. Mandatory requirement for any organization processing HIPAA related data ( Personal Health Information ( PHI )). HIPAA Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act Guidance developed to help private sector entities and critical infrastructure develop an effective risk-based approach to implementing cybersecurity . Provides information security activities, outcomes, references, and detailed guidance necessary for planning a well-functioning information security program. Voluntary Voluntary NIST Cybersecurity Framework A set of requirements which provide a framework for an organization to plan, and assess their security. It has a very specific mechanism. An organization can contract a third party to verify their security controls and so be deemed compliant with 27001 . ISO 27001 and 27002 Security Design Principles Make Compromise Detection Easier: Even if you take all available precautions, there’s still a chance your system will be compromised by a new or unknown attack. To give yourself the best chance of spotting these attacks, you should be well positioned to detect compromise. Reduce The Impact of Compromise: Design to naturally minimize the severity of any compromise. Security Design Principles Establish the context before designing system: Before you can create a secure system design, you need to have a good understanding of the fundamentals and take action to address any identified short-comings. Make Compromise Difficult: Designing with security in mind means applying concepts and using techniques which make it harder for attackers to compromise your data or systems. Make Disruption Difficult: When high-value or critical services rely on technology for delivery, it becomes essential that the technology is always available. In these cases the acceptable percentage of ‘down time’ can be effectively zero. Threat vs. Attack All attacks originate from threats Threat = Potential danger Attack = Actual exploitation attempt Types of Attack These are common cyber attacks that target individuals and organizations. Phishing Ransomware Man-in-the-Middle Denial-of-Service ( DoS ) Organizational Information S ecurity A ssessment I nformation security experts can only offer recommendations ( fixes, mitigations , and so on ). Owner of the business will have to determine what risk is acceptable for their organization. The key to a successful information security program is to properly categorize data and ensure that only those that are authorized to access the data have the rights to do so. Types of Organizational Assessment Internal Assessment Third-party Assessment Security Policy D ifference B etween S ecurity P olicy and Security Mechanism Security Mechanism A statement of what is allowed, and what is not allowed . A method, tool, or procedure for enforcing a security policy. Published works by various professional organizations which attempt to encapsulate the guidance necessary to properly secure an IT system. Different standards have applicability to different industries, such as payment card versus healthcare , but tend to cover the full breadth of applicable system-related components, such as network devices, workstations, servers, software, user interaction with systems, system process interactions, data transmission, and storage. text: FOUNDER’S MESSAGE Pakistan is the 5th most populous country in the world with diverse topography having the highest mountain ranges in the North and Arabian Sea in the South, as a result of which we face diverse nature of emergencies and disasters. This led to the development of integrated Emergency Services in Pakistan, because of which millions of emergency victims have been provided with the right to timely professional emergency care without discrimination. In order to share this diverse experience, knowledge, best practices and to improve coordination amongst international emergency services, the International Rescue Challenge & Conference is being organized in the Emergency Services Academy, Lahore - Pakistan from 21-22 October 2024. This event is a testament to our commitment to enhance international cooperation and knowledge exchange amongst emergency services. It is also an opportunity for firefighters, Paramedics, and Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) Teams from around the world to exhibit their professional skills, share innovative practices in search and rescue, trauma management, firefighting, and collectively advance our understanding and implementation of best practices. We look forward to welcoming the emergency services in the centrally located historic city of Lahore, Pakistan, where we can unite our efforts to enhance global emergency response capabilities. Dr. Rizwan Naseer, SI Secretary, Emergency Services Department/ Commander Pakistan Rescue Team International Rescue Challenge 2024 Lahore Pakistan Page 1 Contents 1 Introduction 3 2 Purpose 3 3 Objectives 4 4 The Challenge 4 5 Composition of Teams 4 6 Logistics Arrangements 5 7 Description of the Event 5 8 Team Position Criteria 11 9 General Instructions / Guidelines 12 10 Annexure 13 International Rescue Challenge 2024 Lahore Pakistan Page 2 1. Introduction As natural disasters, accidents, and humanitarian crises become more common and severe, the need for skilled emergency response teams is greater than ever. The Emergency Services Academy Lahore Pakistan is organizing the International Rescue Challenge to enhance the professional competencies of rescuers to cope with emergencies and disaster challenges, through healthy competition. At the International Rescue Challenge, teams from all over the world will come together to compete in different rescue scenarios. The teams will participate in different competitions that reflect real emergencies, giving them a chance to demonstrate their professional knowledge &skills in the field of search &rescue and emergency management. More than just a competition, the International Rescue Challenge serves as a platform for knowledge exchange, networking, and collaboration among rescue professionals, government agencies, NGOs, and other stakeholders involved in emergency response. It provides a unique opportunity for participants to learn from each other's experiences, share best practices, and build long-lasting partnerships that go beyond geographical boundaries. In short, the International Rescue Challenge is not just a competition—it's a chance for people from all over the world to learn from each other, work together, and make the world safer in times of crisis. 2. Purpose The purpose of organizing the International Rescue Challenge in Pakistan is to improve emergency response capabilities, encourage collaboration among global stakeholders, and strengthen resilience in confronting disasters. Concurrently, the event serves as a pivotal opportunity to spotlight Pakistan's strengths and substantive contributions to the global humanitarian efforts. International Rescue Challenge 2024 Lahore Pakistan Page 3 3. Objectives i. Enhancing Emergency Response Skills: To provide a platform for international rescue teams to demonstrate and improve their skills in various emergency scenarios, including height rescue, well rescue, trauma management and firefighter’s fitness competition. ii. Fostering Collaboration: Facilitate collaboration and knowledge exchange among rescue professionals from different countries, promoting mutual learning and cooperation in the field of emergency response. iii. Promoting Innovation: Showcase innovative technologies, tools, and strategies used in emergency response operations. iv. Capacity Building: Strengthen the capacity of local rescue teams by exposing them to international standards and best practices. 4. The Challenge All international USAR Teams, firefighters and paramedics can participate to showcase their professional knowledge & skills, and physical fitness required to deal with the following scenarios: 1. Height Rescue Challenge 2. Deep Well Rescue Challenge 3. Confined Space Extrication Challenge 4. Trauma Challenge 5. Fitness Challenge 5. Composition of Teams A team comprising of maximum 9 members as per the following:  Height Rescue Challenge 06 Rescue Technicians  Deep Well Rescue Challenge 06 Rescue Technicians  Confined Space Extrication Challenge 06 Rescue Technicians  Trauma Challenge 02 Emergency Paramedics  Fitness Challenge 01 Firefighter/ Rescue Technician Note: The teams may participate in all events or any single event of the challenge as per their expertise or choice. International Rescue Challenge 2024 Lahore Pakistan Page 4 6. Logistics Arrangements All the teams are encouraged to bring their personal protective equipment, fire suits, and essential equipment especially used in rope rescue according to the scenario. However, a fully equipped ambulance with standard supplies including all types of stretchers, complete SCBA sets, Full Body Harness, Static Ropes, Carabiners, Figure of Eight, Ascender, Descender, Tripods & Pulleys, and communication devices, etc. shall be provided by the Emergency Services Academy. 7. Description of the Event A. Height Rescue Challenge i. Sample Scenario The fire broke out in the 10th storey of Red Tower, Lahore at 10:00 AM dated 21st October 2024. According to the initial Information, 02 watchmen are trapped in the building, 01 of them is alive on the 08th floor and the other one is dead on the 07th floor. Stairways and Entry Points of the building are blocked due to fallen debris. Improvised entry methods may be adapted to approach and conduct rescue operations. ii. How to Perform  The team leader shall briefly assign tasks to the members.  The team members shall externally approach the building up to the 2nd floor of the fire tower using standpipes/ extension ladder. Afterward, the staircase is intact and team members shall climb the tower's top (10th floor) using stairs.  The team shall make appropriate anchors on the 10th floor and establish rope lines:  At least one team member to ascend from the ground floor to the 7th floor.  One team member to rappel from 10th floor to 8th floor.  The live victim on the 8th floor shall be secured and safely lowered using the belay technique on the adjacent building. International Rescue Challenge 2024 Lahore Pakistan Page 5  The Team shall search for the dead body, properly secure on a basket stretcher, and safely belay it to the ground floor using rope work.  All team members shall reach the ground floor along with all gear and conduct a hot debrief. iii. SOPs & Ground Rules  The total time to perform for a given scenario is 35 minutes.  The participating team (maximum of 06 members) shall arrive and assemble at the designated area along with all necessary equipment and PPE.  Scenario assessment will be according to the Checklist Attached  Proper communication devices will be used during scenario performance.  The team should be well-versed with safety signals.  Throwing ropes (Lines) and equipment from height is strongly discouraged.  The Scenario will be the same for all participating teams. B. Deep Well Rescue i. Sample Scenario A person fell in the open abandoned well which is approximately 20 feet deep. Certain hazards i.e. smoke: heat, bushes, toxic gases, smell, darkness unstable walls, etc. may be present in the cavity (Deep Well). The victim may be trapped in bushes, injured, and suffocated. Local people surrounded the place and demanded immediate evacuation of the trapped victim to save human life. ii. How to Perform  The participating team (maximum of 06 members) shall assemble at the designated area along with all necessary gear and equipment.  The team members shall make contact with the victim and reassure the victim.  The team shall approach the victim using rescue tripod/Ladder method and double pulley rope work. International Rescue Challenge 2024 Lahore Pakistan Page 6  The rescuer shall extricate the victim from the deep well after properly securing the victim with all necessary measures and provide Basic Life Support if necessary.  All team members shall rehab the equipment, and place and conduct a hot debrief. iii.
